what.heading: Where do uploaded files go?
paragraphs: When you upload a file to Colab, it goes into a folder called `/content/`. Your code finds the file by its **path**: the folder, then the exact filename. This page runs in your browser, not in Colab, so here you'll practice building paths as text, which is where most file mistakes happen.

points.title: The folder
points.text: Uploads land in `/content/`, so a path starts with `/content/`.

points.title: The exact name
points.text: Capital letters, spaces, dashes and the `.pdf` ending all have to match.

points.title: Not forever
points.text: Uploads are deleted when the runtime disconnects, for example after it sits idle. Then upload the file again.

example.heading: What it looks like
example.code:
folder = "/content/"
filename = "sample-sdf-document.pdf"
path = folder + filename
print(path)
example.caption: `path` is "/content/sample-sdf-document.pdf": the folder first, then the filename, letter for letter.

demos.label: Join folder and name
demos.code:
folder = "/content/"
filename = "sample-sdf-document.pdf"
path = folder + filename
print(path)
demos.note: The + sign joins two pieces of text. The slash at the end of /content/ keeps the folder and the name apart.

demos.label: Build it with an f-string
demos.note: The f before the quote lets you put a variable inside {curly braces}. Python swaps in its value.

demos.label: Spot a typo
demos.note: Python compares names letter by letter, so capital letters count. In Colab, a wrong name gives a FileNotFoundError.

demos.label: A missing slash
demos.note: Without the slash, the folder and the name run together into a path that doesn't exist.

try.prompt: You uploaded a file named **Certificate_of_Quality_2025.pdf**. Use an f-string to build its full Colab path in a variable named `path`, then print `path`.
try.starter:
filename = "Certificate_of_Quality_2025.pdf"
# build the full path with an f-string, then print it

checks.hint: Create a variable named path that holds the full path as text, for example path = f"/content/{filename}".
Your path still shows the curly braces as plain text. Put the letter f right before the opening quote: f"/content/{filename}".
Your path should start with the folder /content/, with a slash at the start and a slash at the end.

Your path starts with /content/, but the filename part doesn't match Certificate_of_Quality_2025.pdf exactly. Check capital letters, spaces and the .pdf ending. Writing {filename} inside the f-string copies the name exactly.

try.stdout_hint: Your path is right, but nothing gets printed. Add print(path) on the last line.
